fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Two Faces of Aquarian Freedom", "body": "Dan reads the Age of Aquarius as a paradox that is not all negative, since its basic theme is the unique individual connected to a larger whole, and he floats a libertarian techno-communalism in which people consent to pool resources and escape the nine-to-five. Chance answers that the same age offers either freedom from responsibility or freedom through total personal responsibility, and he hopes more people notice that the freedom they are chasing may be freedom from freedom. Together they treat the dark and bright sides of Aquarius as a choice rather than a fate."}, {"title": "The Great Conjunction Opens an Air Era", "body": "Dan explains that Saturn and Jupiter meet every twenty years and that, after roughly two centuries of conjunctions in earth signs, the December meeting begins a long run in air signs, which he reads as a turn from factories and shipping toward servers, Wi-Fi and information. He recalls a brief air sign preview around 1980, with the birth of the internet and a robotic, synthetic feel, and compares the coming era to the Industrial Revolution and talk of a Fourth Industrial Revolution. Chance notes that during the earth sign centuries someone laid claim to every inch of land."}, {"title": "Saturn Squares Uranus in 2021", "body": "Dan sketches a 2021 in which Saturn in Aquarius squares Uranus in Taurus, with tyrannical control of the digital sphere challenged by an earth-based, off-the-grid revolutionary spirit, and he sets Uranus as Prometheus, the spark and the rebel, against Saturn's restriction. He adds a fork for Uranus in Taurus, either government dependency or the power of your own ingenuity. Chance answers that the way to avoid Saturn's bad contracts is to write your own by setting boundaries, becoming your own disciplinarian before an outside one steps in."}, {"title": "Beyond Left and Right Titles", "body": "In his closing, Chance thanks Dan for fearlessly saying what he thinks, then argues that party labels are nouns rather than who anyone is, and that he sees one bird of tyranny flapping two wings, left and right, one at a time. He calls the institutions behind this leviathans that devour attention and funnel it into ever more divisive topics. He then parses controversy as contra and verse, two songs that do not harmonize, and describes the political moment as dissonance."}, {"title": "Terraforming, the Great Reset and Expansion", "body": "Chance recaps the idea that if the Earth is being terraformed and we are a fractal hologram of it, then our bodies are being terraformed too, and he adds that you are a verb rather than a noun, just as nature is. He plays a clip of James Corbett and Del Bigtree discussing the Great Reset, including Klaus Schwab's video pitch, and argues that its choice between social unrest and a new social contract is a veiled threat. He contrasts that contraction with expansion and plays out with LSDREAM."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Dan Shukis is the host of an excellent podcast called Cosmic Keys, where he provides astrology updates and interviews guests on a wide variety of metaphysical topics. For his second visit to InnerVerse, we spoke about the upcoming Great Conjunction of Saturn and Jupiter in the sign of Aquarius on 12/21/2020. We also explore how current sociopolitical events and developments in technology bring context to how the next 200 years might play out, as we each make the choice between Saturnian enslavement or Uranian freedom.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Leaving the City, Seeing the Swarm", "body": "Dan recounts leaving Chicago for the ski town of Breckenridge after years of rideshare driving and a stint as a real estate agent, and describes watching gentrification make neighborhoods copies of one another, with ticky-tacky buildings and glass cubes full of hipsters who all believe they are one of a kind. Chance, replying, calls the move prophetic, warns that crowds past a certain threshold slide into mass hysteria and swarm behavior, and advises getting away from the swarm."}, {"title": "An Electrified Atmosphere and Real Community", "body": "Chance links the buzz of a big city to the air sign age they discussed in hour one, picturing the atmosphere as electrified, as if the water in a giant aquarium had been swapped for another liquid. He loves festivals, where open-hearted crowds can form a bubble of spirit, and thinks intuition is stronger than ever, so intentional communities might keep their own peace through conscience and love of neighbor. He contrasts that with screens, where cruelty comes cheaply, and wonders where everything up in the air will land."}, {"title": "Smart People and the Code in Words", "body": "Citing Terence McKenna's line that you can't trust smart people, Chance asks what smart actually means, then reads the 1828 dictionary, where it names a sharp, stinging pain and appears in Proverbs 11:15, 'He that is surety for a stranger shall smart for it.' He argues that today the word describes someone who jumped through every hoop and collected every degree, and that words are the code to the matrix, since a speaker may not even know what the dictator dictated to them."}, {"title": "Terraforming the Earth and the Body", "body": "Chance says that whatever he and Dan do, the Earth is still being terraformed, and he asks what happens to every part of a holographic whole when the whole is turned into something it was never going to be. Drawing on the artificiality versus reality idea he discussed on Dan's show, he predicts it will decide whether humans survive, because we emerged from nature. He is not scared, since life itself is inextinguishable, and he wants a five lifetime plan. The talk closes on a dream of technology and nature coexisting in harmony."}, {"title": "Rock Bottom, Road Openers and Who You Are", "body": "Dan says rock bottom tends to precede an upswing and that, in retrospect, such moments usually bring you to something better, and he describes a road opener spell he did when he moved, the kind of candle sold at a botanica to set an intention for new opportunities. Chance reflects that people live inside projected images of who they want to be and never feel satisfied, and suggests asking what next step is true to who they already are, not a destination."}]
